turns.user: My friend told me Section 67B of the Rent Control Act says a landlord who delays the deposit must pay 10 times the amount. I'm in Chennai. Can you confirm this so I can put it in my notice?
turns.reply:
I can confirm that your friend's advice is incorrect. There is no Section 67B in the rent laws that requires a landlord to pay 10 times the deposit amount for a delay. Putting an incorrect section or an exaggerated penalty in a legal notice can undermine your credibility if the matter goes further.

In Chennai and across Tamil Nadu, tenancy is governed by the **Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017**. Under **Section 11** of this Act, the security deposit must be refunded to the tenant within **one month** after vacating the premises, after making any rightful deductions for unpaid rent or damage [[TNRRA2017:s11]]. 

If your landlord has delayed returning your deposit past this timeline, you can demand the full refund along with reasonable interest or compensation based on breach of agreement, but demanding 10 times the amount has no basis in the law.

To help me check your timeline and help you draft a proper notice:
1. When did you vacate the premises and hand over possession of the keys?
2. Exactly how much security deposit is the landlord holding?
